chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Safwan, or a man, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Al-Muzdalifa is the place in the lands of Allah with the most insects. So when it is the night of Al-Tarwiyya, a Caller calls out from the Presence of Allah: 'O group of insects, depart from the delegation of Allah!' He said: 'So they go out into the mountains and fill them, where they are not seen. So when the pilgrims depart, they return.'

key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَة: Al-Muzdalifa, a sacred site in Mecca where pilgrims gather after standing at Arafat

ai.seo_question: What happens to the insects in Al-Muzdalifa during the night of Al-Tarwiyya?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the divine preparation of Al-Muzdalifa, emphasizing that its abundance of insects is not a defect but a temporary state cleared by a specific divine command on the night of Al-Tarwiyya. This miraculous event underscores the concept of 'Wafd Allah' (Delegation of God), illustrating how nature actively accommodates the pilgrims' worship, a theme often linked to the spiritual purity and physical ease required for the rites of Hajj.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Safwan, or a man, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukeyr, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Al-Muzdalifa is a city of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with the most insects. So when it is the night of Al-Tarwiyya, a Caller Calls out from the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>: ‘O group of insects! Go away from the delegations of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!’ 
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So they go out to be in the mountains and they crawl around where they cannot be seen. So when the Pilgims leave, they return’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Safwan or a man from Safwan from ibn Bukayr from his father who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Al-Muzdalifah had more insects than other lands of Allah. On the night of al-Tarwiyah, it was announced from Allah, ‘O insects, move away from where delegations to Allah are about to pass.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The insects move in the hills in a way that they are not seen. When al-Hajj (pilgrims) return, they come back.’”
